request: I'm on the State Board of Health and need to get to the national board conference near Dulles on March 22nd. Cheapest economy, please.

trip.purpose: National association of state boards of health annual conference near Washington Dulles

sign_offs.name: State Health Officer, Mississippi State Department of Health
sign_offs.subject: ATTENDANCE

must_keep.quote: To be eligible for reimbursement at the state rate, the employee must have a W2 or receive the maximum state reimbursement rate allowed as per diem in lieu of salary. This applies to Board and Commissions. When an employee receives a per diem "in lieu of salary", they are considered "officers of the state".
must_keep.why: board members on a per diem in lieu of salary are officers of the state

must_keep.quote: The cardless travel account allows travel-related expenses to be delegated to one person, the Program Coordinator, the designated person responsible for making official business travel arrangements for others, including non-entity employees traveling on official state business. Any travel-related services, such as travel agency fees, airfare, railway, vehicle rental, lodging, lodging deposits, travel-related conference registration, etc., which are normally directly billed can now be billed to this account.
must_keep.why: the cardless account books non-entity travellers on official state business

must_keep.quote: Travelers shall request air, train, bus, hotel, and vehicle rental reservations as far in advance as possible and shall utilize the lowest logical rate available.
must_keep.why: the default: the lowest logical rate available

design_notes: A board member is not an employee, but lines 375-377 make a board member paid the per diem in lieu of salary an officer of the state, and lines 1026-1028 let the cardless account book non-entity travellers on official state business. The lowest logical rate: the Charlotte connection.
